headline: Goalie's Stick Wedges in Boards; Billboard Records First NHL Point
subheadline: *Sponsors demand the LED panel be credited with an assist; the Zamboni has reportedly retained an agent.*
author: Hank Delacroix, Sports Desk
seoTitle: NHL Advertising Board Scores First, Sponsors Demand Points
seoDescription: Satire: an NHL goalie's stick got wedged in the advertising boards, letting Winnipeg score — the first recorded offensive contribution by a rink-side billboard.
sourceEvent: During the Winnipeg Jets' win over the Chicago Blackhawks, goaltender Spencer Knight's stick became wedged between the advertising boards behind his net while he played the puck. Winnipeg's Kyle Connor scored into the exposed net before the stick could be freed.

altHeadlines: Goalie's Stick Signs With Boards, Immediately Records First NHL Point
Winnipeg's Newest Scoring Threat Is Seventy-Two Feet of LED Panelling

body:
WINNIPEG — The National Hockey League confirmed this week that a rink-side advertising board has recorded the first offensive contribution by a piece of arena furniture in league history, after a goaltender's stick became firmly wedged in the signage and an opponent scored into the vacated net.

The incident occurred during the Winnipeg Jets' win over the Chicago Blackhawks, when goaltender Spencer Knight slid his stick between the advertising boards behind his own net while playing the puck. The stick remained there — locked, witnesses say, in premium logo position — while Winnipeg's Kyle Connor deposited the puck into the unguarded goal.

'Our understanding is that the boards made a play on the stick,' said a league official, speaking on condition of anonymity because the NHL rulebook contains no provisions governing furniture. 'Whether that constitutes defensive interference or an assist is currently under review by a committee of lawyers and one extremely tired carpenter.'

Sponsors responded within hours, filing a formal request that the LED panel in question — a glowing advertisement for a regional insurance provider — be credited with a secondary assist, noting that the asset 'generated more scoring than several players earning eight figures.'

'We have spent decades telling clients the boards deliver results,' said a spokesperson for the arena's signage consortium, Dale Whitmore, 44. 'This is the first time the board has delivered them on the ice. We consider that a fulfilled KPI.'

The development has sent shockwaves through the league's front offices. Scouts confirmed Monday that at least six teams have dispatched representatives to evaluate other boards around the league, with one Western Conference club reportedly interested in 'the boards' playoff experience.'

'From a purely statistical standpoint, the board is now a more efficient offensive weapon than roughly a third of the league's bottom-six forwards,' said one hockey analyst. 'It has a hundred per cent shooting accuracy by proxy, zero salary cap hit, and it has never once demanded a trade.'

The NHL Players' Association has opened an inquiry into whether the board requires a contract, a locker, and dental coverage — the last of which was described as 'a formality, given the teeth.'

Rival inanimate objects have also begun asserting eligibility. The goal horn has filed paperwork claiming three assists on crowd energy alone, and the Zamboni — long considered the arena's most dependable performer — has retained an agent and is seeking two-way minutes.

The stick, meanwhile, was eventually freed by arena staff using what was described as 'a firm tug and the dignity of everyone involved.'

At press time, the advertising board had been named the game's third star, declined its post-game interview citing lumens, and was reportedly reviewing an offer to have its own jersey retired in the rafters — directly above where the stick remains in storage.
